paper.title: CO-Bench: Benchmarking Language Model Agents in Algorithm Search for Combinatorial Optimization
paper.venue: AAAI 2026 (per request; the v3 PDF has no venue header)

metric.name: Avg Score (normalized score)
metric.definition_paper: s(x,p) = min{|h(x,p)|,|h*_p|} / max{|h(x,p)|,|h*_p|}, h*_p = pre-computed optimal or best-known objective value; errors/infeasible/timeout -> 0; problem score = mean over test instances; overall = mean over the 36 problems (Eq. 6, Evaluation Metrics, p.3)
metric.actual_implementation: Per-problem config.py norm_score: minimisation -> ref/obj, maximisation -> obj/ref (NOT capped at 1, hence values >1 in tables such as MKP ReEvo 1.0019). Averaging (evaluation/utils.py average_score): mean within each data file, then mean over files (files weigh equally, not instances); any error on a file -> 0 for that file.

references_by_problem_repo.Capacitated warehouse location: hard-coded optimal values per OR-Library cap* file (e.g. cap41 1040444.375; capa-8000 19240822.449); score = ref/cost
references_by_problem_repo.Multidimensional knapsack problem: hard-coded optimal/best-known per instance (mknap1, mknap2, mknapcb1-9); score = profit/ref
references_by_problem_repo.Job shop scheduling: score = lower_bound/makespan, where lower_bound is the LB in the Taillard file header (not BKS/optimum) -> an optimal schedule can score <1
references_by_problem_repo.Flow shop scheduling: score = lower_bound/makespan, Taillard header LB (same caveat)
references_by_problem_repo.Vehicle routing: period routing: hard-coded per file prvp1-10 (e.g. prvp1 547.9); score = ref/distance

metric.other_metrics: Valid Solution (share of problems with all test instances valid), Above Classical, Survival Rate (share of test instances >=99% of reference score) (p.3)

setup.test_time_limit: 10 s per test instance, single CPU core (dual AMD EPYC 7313) (Implementation Details, p.4) [paper]
setup.agent_llm: o3-mini-medium for all agents (Implementation Details p.4; Figure 3 caption p.5) [paper]. Per-problem appendix tables do not repeat the LLM; that they are o3-mini-medium is [inferred] (their averages reproduce Figure 3, see consistency_check).
setup.agent_budget: 64 iteration steps; each step = one candidate code evaluated on the dev set; best-on-dev of the 64 is evaluated on test (p.4) [paper]. Tokens, number of LLM calls per step and wall-clock cost are NOT reported. Dev-evaluation timeout is not stated in the paper; README example uses Evaluator(timeout=10) [repo].
setup.classical_solver: Authors spent ~30 min per problem picking/tuning the best classical solver on the dev set (examples: LKH for TSP, CPLEX for scheduling, Gurobi for MIS) (p.3) [paper]; evaluated under the same 10 s limit ('equivalent time constraints', p.2) [paper]. The specific solver per problem is NOT listed (CPLEX for JSSP/FSSP is [inferred] from 'CPLEX for scheduling'). No classical-solver code in the repo [repo].
setup.agents_evaluated: Direct Answer (15 LLMs), BestOfN, Chain of Experts, Greedy Refinement (cites Shinn 2023 / Madaan 2023 = Reflexion/Self-Refine), FunSearch, EoH, AIDE, ReEvo, MCTS-AHD [paper]. No agent named 'Self-Refine' in CO-Bench; Greedy Refine is the analogue.
setup.per_problem_methods: Appendix tables contain only: Classical Solver, BestOfN, Refine, FunSearch, AIDE, ReEvo, MCTS, EoH. Chain of Experts and the direct-answer LLMs have no per-problem values (only aggregates in Figure 3).

Capacitated warehouse location.source: Appendix 'Problem Description and Scores', Table 7, p.12 [paper]
Capacitated warehouse location.data: OR-Library cap41-cap134 + capa/capb/capc (4 sizes each), 49 files of 1 instance; dev = 12 files -> 37 test instances [repo]

Multidimensional knapsack problem.data: mknap1 (7), mknap2 (48), mknapcb1-9 (30 each); dev indices per file -> test = 4 + 24 + 9x15 = 163 instances [repo]
Multidimensional knapsack problem.note: Values >1 = better than the hard-coded reference (uncapped ratio) [repo/inferred]

Job shop scheduling.data: Taillard tai15_15 ... tai100_20, 8 files x 10; dev 5 per file -> 40 test instances [repo]

Flow shop scheduling.data: Taillard PFSP tai20_5 ... tai500_20, 12 files x 10; dev 5 per file -> 60 test instances [repo]

Vehicle routing: period routing.data: prvp1-prvp10 (Christofides & Beasley 1984), 1 instance each; dev = prvp1,3,5,7,9 -> 5 test instances [repo]
Vehicle routing: period routing.note: Only vehicle-routing problem in CO-Bench (TSP and resource-constrained shortest path are the other routing problems)

CO-Bench.consistency_check: Mean of the 36 appendix tables (my parse): Classical 0.7973, BestOfN 0.7744, Refine 0.8401, FunSearch 0.8423, AIDE 0.7534, ReEvo 0.7741, MCTS 0.7627 -> match Figure 3; EoH 0.8007 vs 0.840 in Figure 3 -> MISMATCH (one of the two is wrong in the paper) [inferred].

paper.title: FrontierCO: Real-World and Large-Scale Evaluation of Machine Learning Solvers for Combinatorial Optimization
paper.arxiv: 2505.16952v3 (9 Mar 2026), 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'
paper.note: v1 (May 2025) had a different title; CFLP/CVRP numbers identical in v1 and v3 [paper]

metric.name: Primal gap (%), lower is better
metric.definition: pg = |cost - c*| / max{|cost|,|c*|}; pg = 1 if infeasible or cost*c*<0; bounded in [0,1] (Eq. 2, p.3). Reported as arithmetic mean +- std over instances; time = geometric mean (x/÷ std). Infeasible -> gap 1 and 3600 s (Sec 3.1 p.5; App. D p.22) [paper]
metric.reference_c_star: BKS from literature/leaderboards, validated with the SOTA solver; where missing/outdated (MDS, CFLP) the designated SOTA solver run up to 2 h (Sec 2.4 p.4-5) [paper]
metric.footnote: Not the routing-literature gap (which can exceed 100%) (footnote 1, p.3) [paper]

setup.time_limit: Max 3600 s per test instance for all solvers (classical, neural, LLM-generated code); single CPU core of dual AMD EPYC 7313; neural on one RTX A6000 (Sec 3.1, p.5) [paper]
setup.llm_agents: FunSearch, Self-Refine (Madaan 2023 / Shinn 2023), ReEvo, following CO-Bench protocol (Sec 3.3 p.6) [paper]
setup.llm: Self-Refine: o4-mini, medium reasoning budget, default sampling (App. C.2 p.21) [paper]. FunSearch and ReEvo: LLM NOT stated; o4-mini medium is [inferred].

budget.Self-Refine: 64 iterations, each gets previous best code + dev results; dev eval timeout 300 s (prompted to write for 3600 s); best-on-dev evaluated on test with 3600 s (C.2 p.21) [paper]
budget.FunSearch: official implementation, prompt adapted; 10 islands, 2 functions per prompt, reset period 2 h, 64 iterations, dev timeout 300 s, test 3600 s (C.2 p.21) [paper]
budget.ReEvo: official implementation; population 10, initial population 4, mutation rate 0.5, 64 iterations, dev timeout 300 s, test 3600 s (C.2 p.21) [paper]

setup.LLM_reported_times: All LLM-agent runtimes are 3600 +-x 1.00 s (code is a generator yielding improving solutions until the limit; prompt C.3 p.21-22) [paper]

CFLP.source: Table 8, p.23 (App. D) [paper]; also Figure 2 p.7 (bars only) and Table 3 p.8 (CFLP-Easy Gurobi 0.00%, SCIP 6.50%, GCNN 3.22%)
CFLP.instances: Easy: 20 largest of Avella & Boccia (2009) Test Bed 1, 1000x1000 (i1000_1..20). Hard: 30 largest of Avella et al. (2009) Test Bed B, 2000x2000 (p2000-2000-31..60) (Table 1 p.4; B.5 p.18) [paper]. Splittable demand ('standard CFLP ... each customer may be served by multiple facilities', B.5) [paper]; config description confirms fractional allocation [repo]
CFLP.reference: Easy: all solved exactly by Gurobi. Hard: literature BKS (Caserta & Voss 2020) worse than Gurobi, so Gurobi re-run 2 h to get references (B.5 p.18) [paper]

CVRP.instances: Easy: 20 Golden et al. (1998), 200-483 customers; route-length constraints of the first eight Golden instances discarded. Hard: 10 Belgium instances of Arnold et al. (2019), 3000-30000 (Table 1 p.4; B.4 p.18) [paper]
CVRP.reference: All BKS from CVRPLib (B.4) [paper]. Evaluator uses unrounded Euclidean distances, while the Belgium BKS in config are integers (e.g. Leuven1 192848) [repo]
CVRP.dev_set: paper: 15 instances, 5 each of 20/100/500 cities (B.4); HF valid_instances has 20/50/100 [repo] -> discrepancy

HGS.hard_time: *3600 ±× 1.00 s (asterisk printed on the hard time only)
